The '''2000–01 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 99th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 69th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It was contested by 18 teams, for the 13th consecutive season since [[1988–89 Serie A|1988–89]].

[[AS Roma|Roma]] won its first ''[[Scudetto]]'' since [[1982–83 Serie A|1982–83]], its third title overall. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] finished second, and these two teams automatically qualified for the first group stage of the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League]]. [[SS Lazio|Lazio]], the defending champions, and [[Parma AC|Parma]] finished third and fourth respectively, to enter the third qualifying round of the same competition. [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]] finished fifth and sixth respectively, and qualified for the [[2001–02 UEFA Cup]] along with [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], the winners of the [[Coppa Italia]]. [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] gained entry into the [[2001 UEFA Intertoto Cup]].

[[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]], [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] and [[AS Bari|Bari]] were automatically relegated to [[Serie B]]. [[Reggina 1914|Reggina]] and [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]] were forced to contest a relegation tie-breaker after finishing level on points, with Verona winning on away goals to relegate Reggina.

==Rule changes==
In the middle of the season, the old quota system was abolished, meaning that each team was no longer limited to having no more than five non-EU players and using no more than three in each match.<ref name=provision>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604164248/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Italians bar non-EU imports|date=2002-07-17|access-date=2010-03-09|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/1005793.stm|title=Milan challenge non-EU rule|date=2000-11-03|access-date=2010-03-09|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==Passport scandal==
Concurrent with the abolition of the quota system, the [[Italian Football Federation]] (FIGC) investigated footballers from South America and Cameroon who had used fake [[passport]]s in order to enable their teams to field them as Europeans. [[Alberto do Carmo Neto|Alberto]], [[Warley Silva dos Santos|Warley]], [[Alejandro Da Silva]] and [[Jorginho Paulista|Jorginho]] of [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]],<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/962023.stm | work=BBC News | title=Fake passport scandal hits Serie A | date=2000-10-08 | access-date=2010-05-23}}</ref> [[Fábio Júnior Pereira|Fábio Júnior]] and [[Gustavo Bartelt]] of Roma,<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/1318504.stm | work=BBC News | title=Lazio hit with passport charges | date=2001-05-08 | access-date=2010-05-23}}</ref> [[Dida (footballer, born 1973)|Dida]] of Milan, [[Álvaro Recoba]] of Inter, [[Thomas Job]], [[Francis Zé]] and [[Jean Ondoa]] of [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], and [[Jeda (footballer)|Jeda]] and [[André Leone]] of Vicenza were all handed bans in July 2001, ranging from six months to one year.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/internationals/players-banned-over-false-passport-scandal-675847.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100206014855/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/internationals/players-banned-over-false-passport-scandal-675847.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 6, 2010 | work=The Independent | location=London | title=Players banned over false passport scandal | first=Frances | last=Kennedy | date=2001-06-28 | access-date=2010-05-23}}</ref> However, most of these bans were subsequently reduced.
